judge: Claude Code subagent, Claude Opus 5.5, fresh

items.label: A
items.critique: Lively opener and a guessing aside feel Nox-like, but the plot is overloaded (garrison business, rival's marching drills, hounds, then a second hook about dead men) and two rewards stacked in one quest; Westwood's quests are plainer and single-minded.

items.label: B
items.critique: Plain cause-and-effect setup (urchin aggravates bats), concrete item ('ruby key'), the petition as reward, and the inconsistent capital on 'Urchin' are all Westwood's slightly loose house style.

items.label: C
items.critique: Exclamatory panic ('worse than the pox!'), the blunt stage direction 'there, through the double doors', and a title-plus-gold reward with 'I insist' read like the campaign.

items.label: D
items.critique: Comic repetition of 'mate', the bathing joke, and the mild 'damn fine spell' are Westwood's broad, cheeky humour; short exclamatory lines.

items.label: E
items.critique: Mixed casing of Urchins, the 'Hmmm... Yes.' beat, and the teleporter hand-off to the next chapter are characteristic; the dark twist told only through a found robe is Westwood's economy.

items.label: F
items.critique: Digits ('3 nights out of 4'), the bounty-season framing, a missing comma in 'Thanks again Wanderer', and 'done the whole shore a great service' sound like a modern writer's flat procedural tone rather than Nox's exclamatory voice.

items.label: G
items.critique: Boastful captain is a fair archetype, but the sidequest-before-the-real-threat logic is contrived, the fixed '80 gold' is repeated, and the thanks is an oddly practical remark about stings with no exclamation or warmth.

items.label: H
items.critique: The pet frog, the '?!' punctuation and the 'Loads and loads of money?' gag answering the silent hero are pure Westwood humour.

items.label: I
items.critique: Backstory comes in the wrong order (the attack, then who sent him), the reward promise is vague, and 'Yay!' plus 'safe in the fold again' is an off register for a Nox villager.

items.label: J
items.critique: Tactical setup (staked goat, barring stable doors, waiting for a signal) is more fiddly than any Nox quest, the bow is promised then handed over with a redundant line, and 'let the mules out to graze' is a writerly flourish.

tells: Westwood's offers are exclamatory and emotional (panic, outrage, pleading) with a single clear goal; the new texts are calmer, more procedural, and pile on circumstantial setup (seasons, schedules, tactics, rivalries).
Westwood leans on broad, slightly silly humour (pet frogs, stolen boots while bathing, the hero's implied demand for money); the new texts have little or only dry humour.

Westwood's thanks lines are short bursts ('My boots!', 'Excellent! You've killed the Urchin.') followed by the reward and often a pointer to the next place; generated thanks drift into flat remarks or redundant restatements of the reward.
Numerals and exact sums ('3 nights out of 4', '80 gold' twice) and modern-feeling words ('Yay', 'bounty this season') mark the new texts.
Westwood's quests use concrete gate items and progression rewards (keys, petitions, titles, access, teleporters); the new texts tend to reward with generic bows and gold.
Overloaded quests (two hooks, two rewards, sidequest-before-the-real-quest logic) read as generated; Westwood keeps one trouble, one fix.
